listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Tuesday, November 3. Here is what matters today. Our lead story. The United States has struck Qeshm Island in Iran, just ahead of the midterm elections, according to the BBC. US officials described the attacks as limited and defensive. The BBC cites CBS, its US partner. Few other details are available yet, so the scale of the strikes is not clear. Now the front page. In tech, the Claude Platform release notes from November second describe message threads for the Messages API, in beta. The server keeps the conversation, so each later request sends only the new messages. The result is smaller requests and a lower time to first token in long conversations and agent loops. In basketball, Alperen Sengun had 26 points, 10 assists and seven rebounds. The Rockets beat the Celtics 109 to 93 and moved into first place in the West. In politics, The Lever reports that a super PAC network funded by Big AI became politically toxic. It stopped donating in the most competitive Congressional races. In Ukraine, Kyiv says Russian bombing killed 29 people at an aid centre in a southern village. Officials say at least nine very large aerial bombs hit the village. Now the sections. In tech, a trending command line tool called agent desktop lets AI agents operate desktop apps. Anthropic also says it is committing a portion of its shares to a new Public Benefit Fund. In politics, The Lever reports that Abdul El-Sayed raised a seven-figure sum after Haley Stevens endorsed Republican Mike Rogers. The Supreme Court also turned down a Justice Department request to step into its dispute with California over voter rolls. In world news, Israel's election was inconclusive, though Prime Minister Netanyahu won the largest number of votes. Also, a US and Russia impasse at the United Nations ended the peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara after 35 years. In sports, Brandon Aiyuk has hired agent Drew Rosenhaus and hopes to return to the NFL. In the UFC, Tom Nolan knocked out Renato Moicano in the third round. In Atlanta, a multifamily project in Blandtown is nearing the end of construction. Georgia also set a midterm record, with more than 2.8 million early votes. In architecture, AEC Magazine asks how to make AI-built software for the building industry safe and accountable. ArchDaily looks at designing for neurodivergent ways of perceiving space. In science, NASA's November skywatching guide covers meteor showers, Mars near Jupiter, and a supermoon. Researchers also report that thawing permafrost has created a new type of large landslide. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: US strikes Iranian island ahead of midterm elections
lead.note: The United States has struck Qeshm Island in Iran, just ahead of the midterm elections, according to the BBC. US officials described the attacks as limited and defensive, the BBC reports, citing CBS, its US partner. Defensive, in this context, is the officials' own word, not an independent finding. The summary gives few other details, so the scale of the strikes and any damage are not yet clear from this item. The timing is what makes the story notable for today, since Americans are voting while military action is in the news. Readers should watch for further official statements and for any response from Tehran, which this item does not describe. For now, the account rests on how US officials characterised the strikes and on reporting from a partner network.
